## Dataset

Describe the public dataset (GEO accession, organism, conditions, number of donors),
and why it suits the question. Pseudobulk DE needs biological replicates, so aim for
at least 3 donors per condition.

## Setup

```{r}
#| message: false
library(Seurat)
library(SingleR)
library(celldex)
library(DESeq2)
library(ggplot2)

obj <- readRDS(params$integrated_rds)
obj
```

## Cell type annotation

Reference-based annotation with SingleR. Check the result against known marker genes,
since automated labels can be wrong for rare or unusual populations.

```{r}
ref  <- celldex::MonacoImmuneData()  # swap for a reference that fits your tissue
pred <- SingleR(
  test   = GetAssayData(obj, layer = "data"),
  ref    = ref,
  labels = ref$label.main
)
obj$cell_type <- pred$labels
DimPlot(obj, group.by = "cell_type", label = TRUE, repel = TRUE)
```

## Pseudobulk differential expression

Cells from one donor are not independent replicates. Aggregating counts per
sample and cell type, then testing with a bulk method, avoids inflated p-values.

Aggregate with `scuttle::aggregateAcrossCells()`, which keeps the sample metadata
as `colData` instead of encoding it in column names.

```{r}
library(SingleCellExperiment)
library(scuttle)

sce <- as.SingleCellExperiment(obj, assay = "RNA")
pb  <- aggregateAcrossCells(sce, ids = colData(sce)[, c("sample", "cell_type")])
pb  # columns = sample x cell type; colData carries condition and donor
```

Choose the design to match the study. If each donor appears in both conditions, use
`~ donor + condition` (paired). If each donor contributes one sample (as in an
unpaired case/control study), donor is nested in condition and the design is
`~ condition`. Skip cell types with too few cells per sample to aggregate reliably.

```{r}
#| eval: false
run_de <- function(counts, coldata, design = ~ condition) {
  dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(counts, coldata, design = design)
  dds <- DESeq(dds)
  results(dds)
}
```

## Interpretation notes

- Which cell types respond most, and do the top genes make biological sense?
- How did Harmony affect mixing of donors, and did it preserve the condition effect?
- Limitations: ambient RNA not removed, annotation not manually curated.
